mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 such labor strength months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 20-day return during neutral labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% month-over-month indicates accelerating economic demand, which typically precedes equity market expansion and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 10 such INDPRO spikes, the 5-day forward return is negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months suggests a cooling demand environment that reduces growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods matching the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during high-inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 1% for 3 months, it indicates accommodative policy that lowers real discount rates, thereby supporting higher expected equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In low-rate regimes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 60-day return during normal-rate regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a softening labor market, which can erode consumer and business confidence and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: During 10 such cooling episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than during expansionary periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) for two months signals supply-side softness that can depress growth forecasts and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 2 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 such supply-side weak months, the 20-day forward return is not significantly worse than during balanced supply cycles (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 4% while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 2%, it indicates a policy mismatch that can amplify recessionary expectations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2%
failure_condition: During 10 such misalignment events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically lower than during aligned policy windows (p > 0.05).
